source.title: Deep Networks and the Multiple Manifold Problem
source.authors: Sam Buchanan; Dar Gilboa; J. Wright

record.file_problem: Text is cut off at the start of Appendix E.3; the supplied paper is incomplete.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves a random-initialization gradient-descent result for perfect classification on a synthetic manifold problem, using a theoretical analysis rather than testing the listed benchmark settings.
record.gate_note: The theorem and proposition below are the paper's own results. CIFAR benchmarks, corrupted or random labels, convolutional networks, and the listed initialization, depth, learning-rate, normalization, and width comparisons are not tested.
record.test_reason: The study proves classification guarantees for fully connected ReLU networks on structured manifolds. None of its results tests the architectures, tasks, or comparisons named in V1–V6. A theoretical convergence result alone does not establish a test of these versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors establish rapid perfect manifold classification under stated assumptions, interpreting depth as a fitting resource and width as a concentration resource. Explicit certificate construction covers coaxial circles; extension to general curves remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes vanilla gradient descent on a synthetic manifold classification problem with a fully connected ReLU network and squared loss; it does not use the listed benchmark recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The guarantee depends on data geometry and certificate existence, network depth and width, sample count, and a suitably small step size.

fits_no_version.finding: Under certificate, geometry, depth, width, sample-size, and small-step-size assumptions, random-initialization gradient descent perfectly separates two one-dimensional manifolds; an explicit certificate is constructed for coaxial circles.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently deep and wide fully connected ReLU networks trained by gradient descent can achieve perfect manifold classification with high probability in the specified structured-data setting.

record.problems: The main separation guarantee is conditional on certificate existence; the explicit construction covers only the specified two-circles geometry. Results are theoretical guarantees rather than empirical benchmark measurements. The supplied text is truncated.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks trained with SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels, and the smaller-model, early-stopping, and regularization comparisons.
Spurious-minimum frequencies in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of one or two additional student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, special tanh initializations, or Fixup.
Effects of alternative initializations on training speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights. Appendix A.3 explains the chosen scaling but supplies no such comparison.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature adaptation, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence below the threshold. The guarantees require small step sizes.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

rows.subject: deep fully-connected ReLU network
rows.size_stated: depth L ≥ C1 max{Cμ∞ log⁹(1/δ) log²⁴(Cμ∞ n₀ log(1/δ)), κ²Kλ²/cλ²}; width n = C2 L⁹⁹ log⁹(1/δ) log¹⁸(Ln₀); N ≥ L¹⁰
rows.operation_detail: Vanilla gradient descent with constant step size τ, from randomly initialized weights, on the finite-sample squared-loss objective.

conditions.value: N i.i.d. samples from two one-dimensional manifolds; coaxial two-circles geometry with r ≥ 1/2
A certificate satisfying the theorem's stated bounds exists

rows.measure: Perfect classification: the trained classifier separates both manifolds.
rows.value: Theorem 1 guarantees separation at iteration ⌊L³⁹⁄⁴⁴/(nτ)⌋ with probability at least 1−δ; for the two-circles geometry, combining with Proposition 1 gives probability at least 1−4δ.
rows.uncertainty: Probability guarantees: at least 1−δ in Theorem 1 and at least 1−4δ for the two-circles setting.
rows.note: Analytical guarantee, not an empirical benchmark result. The row measures perfect classification on the paper's manifold setting; none of the listed versions specifies this setting.
rows.check: The separation guarantee is valid under the stated assumptions but cannot determine any listed version. Distinguish Theorem 1's conditional guarantee for general regular curves from the explicit two-circles result, which additionally requires L ≥ CΔ⁻¹ and 1/2 ≤ r < 1. The combined separation probability is at least 1−4δ.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Discusses gradient-based training, depth, width and initialization without testing any listed version.

source_check.notes: Theorem 1 requires a certificate; Proposition 1 constructs one for coaxial circles. The combined separation guarantee is at least 1−4δ under the stated assumptions. The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased.
